prose.favour: The case in its favour rests mostly on the balance sheet: profit covers interest costs 22.9 times over. Also in its favour: debt is lower than shareholders' equity (debt-to-equity 0.28); free cash flow is 6.9% of the market value, a solid cash return; and return on capital employed is 17.8%, a strong return on the money in the business. Other areas on this side: cash flow and the balance sheet, what the price asks for the earnings, risk.
prose.against: The case against rests mostly on the recent price trend: the share price is 23.0% lower than a year ago. Also against it: over the past year the share did 22.8 percentage points worse than the Nifty 50; the share price is 31% below its 52-week high; and growth scores only 26 of 100 against the comparison pool. Other areas on this side: growth, price behaviour.
prose.weighing: Weighing them: 8 points in favour and 6 against give more points in favour. The pool score is 56 of 100. The side that carries most weight is the balance sheet. That gives an educational rating of Hold with high confidence. This is a rule-based reading of the evidence above, not a prediction.
